title: Systems Folio — Design-Research Feature
description: A two-pane design-research spread modeled on IDEO journal aesthetics: a hairline-framed system diagram anchors the left half while a 24pt italic pull quote with em-dash attribution anchors the right. Pale paper stock, charcoal body type, and a single tomato-red accent reserved exclusively for the diagram keep the page arguing, not decorating.
philosophy: This template exists for the researcher who needs the layout to carry an argument, not perform one. It refuses decorative fills, photographic texture, and typographic novelty — the hairline frame around the diagram is the only structural ornament permitted. The single accent color belongs to the diagram alone, so the reader's eye is trained to read system before sentiment. It is made for internal essays, process retrospectives, and the kind of journal spread that gets pinned above a studio whiteboard.
goodFor: Design research retrospectives and methodology essays
3-line italic pull quotes with named researcher attribution
System-diagram explainers paired with dense analytical prose
Internal studio journals and design-sprint post-mortems
avoidFor: Customer-facing sales or product marketing decks
Photography-led editorial spreads requiring full-bleed imagery
Large-room presentations where hairline rules and 24pt type lose legibility
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide opens like the recto of a printed design-research folio — restrained, deliberate, slightly austere. The left zone is structured silence: a precise hairline rectangle with generous interior breathing room signals 'diagram lives here' without filling it decoratively. The right zone carries the argument — title stacked tightly above a thin horizontal rule, subtitle set smaller beneath, and an attribution or studio name anchoring the lower third. The single accent color appears only as the hairline frame stroke, training the eye to read structure before sentiment. Avoid centered symmetry, gradient washes, photographic overlays, and any decorative fill that would make the slide perform rather than argue.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a strict two-pane split: cols 1–5 hold a hairline-bordered rectangular zone acting as the system-diagram placeholder, left-bled to the 7% outer margin; cols 6–12 carry the deck title (stacked over a thin rule), subtitle, and a researcher or studio credit line flush-left at mid-height. No header band; a folio slug and date sit bottom-right in cols 11–12. The hairline frame on the left is the sole structural ornament — everything else is text on pale ground.

examples.promptCore: The spread feels like a page pulled from a rigorous studio journal — austere, purposeful, and structured to carry an argument rather than perform one. Left and right halves hold equal visual mass but speak in different registers: the diagram reads as evidence, the italic pull quote as interpretation, and the body prose as the connective tissue between them. The single accent color lives exclusively inside the diagram's structural marks, conditioning the reader's eye to encounter system before sentiment. Avoid any decorative fill, photographic warmth, illustrative flourish, or compositional gesture that exists only to relieve the density — the restraint is the aesthetic.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid split at col 6; left pane (cols 1–6) contains the hairline-bordered system diagram with roughly 6% inner padding — the frame itself is the only structural ornament permitted. Right pane (cols 7–12) stacks a large italic pull quote in the upper third, an em-dash attribution line immediately below, then a block of dense analytical body copy filling the lower two-thirds. Outer margin holds approximately 7% breathing room on all four edges, with a discreet folio number anchored bottom-right outside the live text area. Hierarchy is established through size contrast and hairline rule weight alone — no background fill, no header band, no texture of any kind.
